_comment: Indian music artists the user asks for by name, with the Latin-script spellings an
English-biased recogniser produces instead. Read by alfred_computer_use/artists.py.
`name` is the canonical Spotify spelling: it is what gets searched for and what goes
into whisper's initial prompt. `aka` are other right names for the same artist.
`wrong` are mis-hearings -- evaluation data and lookup keys, NEVER prompt terms (the
prompt budget is 50 terms, stt._WHISPER_BIAS_MAX).
`rank` orders artists by how likely they are to be asked for, 1 first. It decides who
fits in the prompt budget before any usage has been recorded, and it decides whether
an ordinary phrase on its own ('cd mode') may be read as an artist.
`ordinary_words` are words said for reasons that have nothing to do with music:
English, first names and surnames, places, everyday Hindi. A variant made only of
these is never applied by the safe tier. An earlier attempt without this rewrote
5.2% of real song titles -- 'play mann meri jaan' became the artist 'Jaani'.
`outsiders` are famous names that are NOT in the catalogue but sound like somebody
who is: artists, actors, films. Heard exactly, no part of one becomes an artist;
heard nearly, one of them close to a catalogue artist makes similarity refuse. Add
one when a real name keeps turning into its neighbour ('mika singh' -> MixSingh).
`name_words` are given names, surnames and gods' names people commonly have. Heard
near an artist, one of them is somebody else unless it is one of that artist's own
words respelled ('diljeet' is Diljit; 'kiran' is not Karan, 'kaur' is not Khaira), so
similarity refuses: 'nimrat kaur', 'ankur tewari' and 'shankar mahadev' stay as said.
They only restrain similarity; a listed mis-hearing is still applied as listed.
Adding a variant: lower case, one spelling per entry. If every word in it is a real
word, add the missing ones to `ordinary_words` too, then run tests/test_artists.py --
it replays 175 everyday commands and 586 real song titles against both tiers.

mechanisms.ASP: aspirated stop flattened: bh->b, gh->g, kh->k/c, dh->d/th, jh->j, ph->f
mechanisms.RET: retroflex -> alveolar, and voicing flips (Sidhu->Sudo, Badshah->Batshah)
mechanisms.VOW: Punjabi/Hindi vowels: au=/ɔ/ not /aʊ/, schwa deletion, long/short collapse
mechanisms.SPL: split into English words (Sidhu Moose Wala -> Sidemot, Talwiinder -> Tall Winder)
mechanisms.ENG: pulled to a known English/proper noun (Karan->Quran, Jaani->Johnny, Naezy->Nazi)
mechanisms.GEM: gemination and numerology spellings (Harrdy, Talwiinder, Kakkar)
